title: Azure Governance, Network and Operations Assurance Capstone
summary: Integrate Azure scope, RBAC, Policy, network segmentation, observability and evidence-first troubleshooting into one production cloud assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit an Azure estate with inconsistent scope ownership, inherited RBAC and Policy controls, uncertain VNet/NSG intent and fragmented monitoring evidence. Leadership requires a defensible operational-readiness and governance decision before a major workload migration.
business_context: The platform must balance workload-team autonomy with enterprise governance, least privilege, network isolation and observable operations.
technical_constraints: Assessment is read-only. Role assignments, policy exemptions, NSG/route edits, diagnostic-setting changes, restarts and deployments require separate approved change authority.
functional_requirements: Map management-group, subscription and resource-group ownership and inherited governance controls.
Reconcile RBAC and Policy so authorization and compliance failures are diagnosed separately.
Review VNet, subnet, route and NSG design for segmentation intent and hidden dependencies.
Assess Azure Monitor, Log Analytics and alert coverage for meaningful operational evidence.
Build an evidence-first decision tree for access, policy, network and telemetry incidents.
Produce a prioritized cloud-governance and operations backlog with owners, validation and rollback boundaries.
non_functional_requirements: No production mutation during evidence collection.
Conclusions must cite Azure-native evidence and scope context.
Recommendations must preserve least privilege and separation of duties.
implementation_plan: Baseline scope and ownership.
Reconcile access and policy inheritance.
Review network segmentation and effective-path assumptions.
Review monitoring and alert evidence.
Tabletop a multi-layer Azure incident and produce a prioritized remediation plan.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend Azure governance and operational readiness with traceable scope, access, policy, network and telemetry evidence.
rollback_dr: Any later control-plane or network remediation requires approved rollback and post-change validation.

assessment_rubric.governance_reasoning: Separates RBAC, Policy and ownership correctly.
assessment_rubric.network_reasoning: Distinguishes routing, filtering, DNS and workload health.
assessment_rubric.change_safety: Keeps all mutation behind explicit approval.

title: Secure CI/CD, Artifact and Release Governance Capstone
summary: Integrate repository governance, pipeline security, immutable artifacts, environment controls, observability and recovery into a production delivery assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit a delivery platform where branch protection, service-connection scope, artifact provenance and production approvals are inconsistent. A release-readiness review is required before teams are allowed to scale automated deployment.
business_context: Delivery speed is valuable only if source, build, artifact, deployment authority and runtime evidence remain traceable and recoverable.
technical_constraints: Assessment is read-only. No policy bypass, force push, secret exposure, privilege expansion, protected-environment mutation or production deployment is allowed.
functional_requirements: Trace representative changes from work item or requirement through commit, PR, build, artifact and deployment evidence.
Assess branch permissions/policies and identify bypass or force-push risk.
Assess pipeline stages, immutable artifact flow and dependency provenance.
Review service connections, variable groups, secure resources and environment checks for least privilege and separation of duties.
Correlate deployment success with runtime health and define rollback/roll-forward decision criteria.
Produce a prioritized delivery-control backlog with owners, measurable gates and emergency-path governance.
non_functional_requirements: Secrets never appear in evidence packs.
Build and deployment authority remain separated where required.
Emergency delivery paths must be explicit and reviewable.
implementation_plan: Baseline repository controls.
Trace pipeline and artifact provenance.
Review privileged delivery resources and environment checks.
Review runtime verification and recovery evidence.
Tabletop a failed/urgent release and produce the governance backlog.
validation: Passes when the learner can demonstrate an auditable commit-to-runtime chain with bounded privilege, independent gates and recovery criteria.
rollback_dr: Any release-control change or production deployment requires separately approved rollback or roll-forward planning.

assessment_rubric.recovery: Defines observable post-deployment and rollback criteria.

title: AWS Governance, Network and Evidence-Driven Operations Capstone
summary: Integrate AWS Organizations, IAM, VPC controls, CloudWatch and CloudTrail into a production cloud governance and incident-assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit a multi-account AWS estate with inconsistent role design, unclear SCP intent, fragmented VPC controls and incomplete incident attribution. Leadership requires a cloud-governance and operational-assurance decision before onboarding additional workloads.
business_context: The estate must reduce blast radius through account boundaries, temporary credentials, layered network controls and durable audit evidence.
technical_constraints: Assessment is read-only. IAM/SCP changes, access-key creation, route/security-group/NACL changes, trail changes, resource restarts and deployments require separate approval.
functional_requirements: Map account/OU ownership and distinguish organization guardrails from granted permissions.
Assess workforce/workload access for federation, roles, temporary credentials and least privilege.
Review VPC addressing, routes, security groups and network ACLs as separate control layers.
Assess CloudWatch telemetry and CloudTrail attribution coverage for incident operations.
Build a layered decision tree for access, connectivity and observability failures.
Produce a prioritized AWS governance and operations backlog with explicit owners and change boundaries.
non_functional_requirements: No root or long-lived credentials are introduced for troubleshooting.
Evidence must identify account, Region, role and resource scope.
Recommendations preserve least privilege and multi-account blast-radius controls.
implementation_plan: Baseline accounts, roles and guardrails.
Review VPC and filtering layers.
Review telemetry and audit evidence.
Tabletop an IAM/network incident using provider-native evidence.
Produce prioritized governance, observability and resilience actions.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend AWS governance and incident readiness with traceable identity, account, network, telemetry and API-attribution evidence.
rollback_dr: Any later IAM, Organizations or network mutation requires approved rollback and post-change verification.

assessment_rubric.identity_governance: Separates IAM grants, boundaries and SCP guardrails.
assessment_rubric.network_reasoning: Separates routes, security groups, NACLs and workload health.
assessment_rubric.auditability: Uses CloudTrail and CloudWatch for different evidence roles.
assessment_rubric.change_safety: Avoids privilege escalation as a diagnostic shortcut.

title: Hybrid and Multi-cloud Governance, Connectivity and Recovery Capstone
summary: Integrate cross-platform ownership, provider-native authorization, hybrid connectivity, telemetry and recovery dependencies into one multi-cloud assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit an application spanning on-premises infrastructure, Azure and AWS. Ownership, route authority, DNS dependencies, federated sign-in and recovery responsibilities are only partially documented. Leadership requires a resilience and governance decision before expansion.
business_context: The service depends on multiple control planes; common operating standards must not erase provider-native authorization, connectivity or recovery truth.
technical_constraints: Assessment is read-only. Federation, RBAC/IAM, route advertisements, VPN/private circuits, firewalls, Arc connectivity, DNS forwarding and production workloads are not changed.
functional_requirements: Map workload ownership and authoritative control planes across on-premises, Azure and AWS.
Separate federation from provider-native authorization and document least-privilege boundaries.
Reconstruct the end-to-end network path including circuits/tunnels, BGP/static routes, filters/firewalls and DNS.
Correlate central telemetry with Azure-, AWS- and on-premises-native evidence.
Define degraded-mode operations if a central management plane becomes unavailable.
Design a recovery exercise that restores identity, DNS, transit, secrets/certificates, data, monitoring and business-service health rather than compute alone.
non_functional_requirements: No single dashboard is treated as the sole source of truth.
Recovery plans include shared dependencies and management-plane outage scenarios.
implementation_plan: Baseline ownership and identities.
Map connectivity and DNS end to end.
Correlate telemetry across platforms.
Tabletop management-plane and cross-cloud connectivity failures.
Produce a prioritized governance and recovery backlog.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend a cross-cloud operating model, diagnose layered connectivity failures and produce a complete shared-dependency recovery plan.
rollback_dr: Any later identity, route, tunnel, firewall or management-agent change requires explicit rollback and cross-platform validation.

assessment_rubric.boundary_reasoning: Preserves provider-native identity and policy semantics.
assessment_rubric.connectivity: Diagnoses transport, routing, filtering, DNS and workload layers separately.
assessment_rubric.operability: Retains provider-native degraded-mode access and evidence.
assessment_rubric.recovery: Restores shared dependencies, not compute alone.
